title: the tester runs a proof in a Windows job with no console, so a proof's scratch process dies with the run and opens no window
intention: On Windows the tester starts each proof in a job object that kills every descendant when the run ends, and with no console window, so a scratch process a proof starts dies with that proof and opens no window; the sites that spawn are not edited.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: on Windows test_shim_starts_the_loop left two ground_loop python.exe running and never returned (90 minutes); batch 1 of ten other proofs left none
traces_to: Law 3 (the leak was measured before it was fixed); Law 7 (the nt note in kill_what_it_started was an admission, now it is a kill); Law 4 (physics in the runner, not a rule each proof must remember); CP4.
how: In cairn/devices/tester/runs.py add run_owned(argv, **kw): on posix it is subprocess.run unchanged; on nt it creates a job (ctypes kernel32) with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, starts the child with creationflags CREATE_NO_WINDOW, assigns it to the job at once, waits like subprocess.run (timeout kills the tree), then closes the job. kill_what_it_started on nt stops returning the 'cannot be enumerated' note and returns the job kill it did. cairn/devices/tester/device.py uses run_owned at the two subprocess.run sites that start a proof or an exec command. Red-first proof cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_windows_run_ends_what_it_started.py: on any host it mocks the kernel32 calls and asserts the job limit, the assignment, the creationflags and that posix is untouched. The tooth that really spawns a grandchild on Windows is NOT written, because a proof that starts Windows processes waits on Q#92 (CAIRN_PROOF_MAY_SPAWN, Akien's); that tooth is Linux-only and the Windows result is a hand measurement with the leak table's before/after snapshot.

clauses.claim: on nt the tester starts a proof with CREATE_NO_WINDOW inside a job that carries KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, and closing the job ends every descendant
on posix run_owned is subprocess.run with the same arguments, and the proof run is unchanged
device.py has no subprocess.run left at the proof-run and exec sites; both go through run_owned
kill_what_it_started on nt no longer answers that environments cannot be enumerated

decisions.text: D1: the fix at cairn/devices/tester/runs.py, cairn/devices/tester/device.py
D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.

measured.saw: on Windows test_shim_starts_the_loop left two ground_loop python.exe running and never returned (90 minutes); batch 1 of ten other proofs left none
measured.how: per-proof before/after process and conhost snapshots from a scratch script, one proof at a time

measured.saw: runs.kill_what_it_started returns 'none: process environments cannot be enumerated on Windows' on nt; device.py:726 and :970 call subprocess.run with no creationflags
NOT measured: that a job object kills a ground_loop started with DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP (breakaway is off by default, so it should); the Windows run of the real spawn waits on Q#92
